- MSA: I pulled the MSA you sent; we have an internal redline template we'll run against yours. I'll route to Legal (cc'ing Marissa) for a focused review on indemnity, liability cap, and data handling clauses.
- PO/EDI: Attached is an internal mapping worksheet request (I will upload the mapping sheet to Drive). Key fields we need from your PO: PO number, line item IDs, unit of measure, ship-to location ID, tax elements, and remit-to GL code. For EDI we ask for an ASN/856 cadence or confirmation process.
- Timeline: legal review turnaround target 48 hours for a callout of high-risk items; portal provisioning we can request immediately, provisioning typically takes 3-5 business days after we confirm vendor profile details.

Next steps: 
1) Marissa (Legal) to review MSA redline + provide a short list of risk items.
2) Kim to coordinate procurement field mapping and provide a completed Ariba/Coupa template by EOD Wed.
3) Alex to open the vendor enrollment in Ariba once mapping is confirmed.

Can we target a legal summary by Wed 6/16 and portal enrollment started by 6/17?

Thanks — I'll flag any blocking items as they arise.

— Alex Martinez

Alex / Team — reviewed the attached redline and prioritized comments below (summary for procurement):

1) Liability cap: propose keeping the contract cap at the greater of $1M or 2x fees for the first 12 months. BlueRidge's redline removes the cap entirely — that's a non-starter.
2) Indemnity: remove broad third-party carveouts tied to regulatory fines; limit indemnity to willful misconduct and negligence + IP infringement. Recommend a mutual indemnity for IP.
3) Data handling / audit logs: we can provide SOC-2 summary and a scoped audit rights clause — offer quarterly snapshot reports and 30 days' notice for on-site audits; push back on unrestricted audit access.
4) Termination for convenience: counter to 90 days notice (BlueRidge asks 30) — recommend 60 days.
5) Payment terms: Net 45 is acceptable; finance confirmed we can accept Net 45 for enterprise accounts but will require a finance-approval ticket (I've looped in KarThik for that queue).

I've attached a one-page redline summary as a PDF and a draft counterlanguage snippet you can paste into procurement communications. If procurement insists on removing the liability cap, escalate to leadership.

Attachments: MSA_Legal_Summary_BR_v1.pdf, MSA_Counterlanguage_snippets.txt

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
